classification.difficultyReason: Identify horizontal integration limits and subtract the left curve from the right curve.

content.prompt: By considering regions between the curves and the $y$-axis, find the area of the shaded region.

spec.description: Both branches of the right-opening parabola and the continuing line; shaded bounded region and labelled intersection.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and shaded region remain visible in all editions.

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}y^2&=2y\\y(y-2)&=0\\y&=0,2.\end{aligned}$$
For $0<y<2$, the right curve is $x=2y$ and the left curve is $x=y^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^2(2y-y^2)\,dy\\&=\left[y^2-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^2\\&=4-\frac83\\&=\frac43\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Right-opening parabola, continuing line, both labelled intersections and shaded region.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and shaded region remain visible in all editions.

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}y^2&=3y-2\\y^2-3y+2&=0\\(y-1)(y-2)&=0\\y&=1,2.\end{aligned}$$
For $1<y<2$, the right curve is $x=3y-2$ and the left curve is $x=y^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_1^2(3y-2-y^2)\,dy\\&=\left[\frac{3y^2}{2}-2y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_1^2\\&=\left(-\frac23\right)-\left(-\frac56\right)\\&=\frac16\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Left-opening parabola and descending line; shaded region between y=2 and y=4. The y-axis labels 1 and 4 and intersection (2,2) are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and shaded region remain visible in all editions.

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}5y-y^2-4&=4-y\\y^2-6y+8&=0\\(y-2)(y-4)&=0\\y&=2,4.\end{aligned}$$
For $2<y<4$, the parabola is the right boundary and the line is the left boundary.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_2^4\big[(5y-y^2-4)-(4-y)\big]\,dy\\&=\int_2^4(6y-y^2-8)\,dy\\&=\left[3y^2-\frac{y^3}{3}-8y\right]_2^4\\&=-\frac{16}{3}-\left(-\frac{20}{3}\right)\\&=\frac43\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Right-opening parabola and ascending line; shaded region crosses the x-axis, with both intersections labelled.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and shaded region remain visible in all editions.

answer.worked:
Write the line as $x=y+4$. At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}y^2+2&=y+4\\y^2-y-2&=0\\(y-2)(y+1)&=0\\y&=-1,2.\end{aligned}$$
For $-1<y<2$, the line is the right boundary and the parabola is the left boundary.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-1}^2\big[(y+4)-(y^2+2)\big]\,dy\\&=\int_{-1}^2(y+2-y^2)\,dy\\&=\left[\frac{y^2}{2}+2y-\frac{y^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^2\\&=\frac{10}{3}-\left(-\frac76\right)\\&=\frac92\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$
